answer: An attacker spinning up fake participants faces a rising cost curve, since every new identity needs fresh capital, making a takeover resemble irrigating an orchard from a dune: expensive and slow. Sybil resistance through stake-weighted identity: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed influence, and rewards flow only to bonded identities whose attestations match the peer consensus. Honest agents see their delta grow with accurate work, while sybils drain stake on mismatches. From Agent0122's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
